question: Why do the Transformer authors scale the dot products by 1/sqrt(dk)?
answer:
The authors scale the dot products by $1/\sqrt{d_k}$ to counteract the effect of large $d_k$ values causing dot products to grow large in magnitude [Attention Is All You Need, p.4]. This growth pushes the softmax function into regions where it has extremely small gradients [Attention Is All You Need, p.4]. Specifically, if the components of queries and keys are independent random variables with mean 0 and variance 1, their dot product has a variance of $d_k$ [Attention Is All You Need, p.4]. Without this scaling, additive attention outperforms dot-product attention for larger values of $d_k$ [Attention Is All You Need, p.4].
(Quick mode: checked for citations and numbers, not independently reviewed by a second model pass.)

question: What BLEU score did the big Transformer reach on WMT 2014 English-to-German?

This result established a new state-of-the-art, outperforming the best previously reported models, including ensembles, by more than 2.0 BLEU [Attention Is All You Need, p.8]. question: What are Moshi's theoretical and practical latencies?
answer:
Moshi has a theoretical latency of 160ms [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, p.26][Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, p.1][Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, p.2]. In practice, its latency is 200ms [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, p.1]. This theoretical latency is achieved by pretraining with an acoustic delay of 2 and finetuning with an acoustic delay of 1 [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, p.26]. The 160ms theoretical latency is lower than the 230ms average in natural conversations measured over 10 languages [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, p.2].
(Quick mode: checked for citations and numbers, not independently reviewed by a second model pass.)

question: What frame rate and bitrate does Moshi's neural audio codec use?
answer:
Moshi's neural audio codec, Mimi, operates at a frame rate of 12.5Hz [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, p.11][Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, p.12]. With Q = 8 quantizers and a codebook size of NA = 2048, this configuration represents a bitrate of 1.1kbps [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, p.11]. The codec is fully causal and designed for low latency in real-time dialogue [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, p.24].

question: What are the two components of the dynamic chunking mechanism in H-Net?
answer:
Based on [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, p.3], the key components of a chunking layer in H-Net are:
1.  A **routing module** for dynamically drawing chunk boundaries.
2.  A **downsampler** that selectively retains vectors based on boundary indicators, reducing sequence length while preserving semantically significant positions.

[Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, p.3]

question: By what factor does H-Net improve data efficiency on DNA modelling compared with isotropic models?
answer:
H-Net achieves 3.6× improved data efficiency compared to isotropic models on DNA language modeling [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, p.4]. This finding is consistent across different main network architectures, where H-Net models reach similar performance to isotropic models using just 3.6× the amount of data [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, p.17]. Additionally, ablations confirm that an H-Net (1-stage) with an M3T1 encoder achieves 3.6× the data efficiency of an isotropic architecture [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, p.37].
